title: Temperature
subtitle: The model’s “boldness” knob
mission: Make the model finish “The cat climbed onto the…” as predictably as possible. Then make it lose the plot.

predict.question: guess before you run! At temperature 0, if you run it 10 times, what comes out?

feedback.right: spot on! At temperature 0 there is no lottery: the model always takes the most likely word. Ten runs, ten “roof”.
feedback.wrong: close! Run it 10 times and notice: always “roof”. At temperature 0 there is no lottery, the model always takes the favorite.
feedback.skipped: you skipped the guess, sneaky. No worries: run it 10 times and notice that at temperature 0 it’s always “roof”.

coach.ui: guess noted. Keep temperature at 0, tick “Repeat 10 times” and hit the orange button.
coach.cmd: guess noted. Run the command below with --times 10 at the end: ten answers in one go.

tryNext.ui: Now drag the temperature to 1.5 and run 10 times again. Compare both runs in the scene.
tryNext.cmd: Now switch to --temp 1.5 and run 10 times again. Notice the scene changes as you type, before you even run.

why.simples:
Look at the bag of marbles in the scene: every marble is a word. “Roof” has loads of marbles; “microwave” has just one.
Temperature is how hard you shake the bag before grabbing the top marble. Temperature 0: no shaking, and the top one is always “roof”. High temperature: the bag turns into a blender, and even the rare marble can rise.
why.dev:
For every possible token, the model returns a score (logit, z). Before softmax, each score is divided by the temperature T.
T below 1 stretches the gaps between scores (a “peaky” distribution); T above 1 flattens it. T = 0 becomes argmax, a.k.a. greedy decoding. Then one token is sampled from that distribution.
why.especialista:
Temperature isn’t “creativity”: it’s sampling entropy. Use T near 0 for extraction, classification and tool calls; 0.7 to 1 for open-ended text.
T = 0 does not guarantee bit-identical output: batching and GPU floating point can vary. The ceiling depends on the API (0–1 on some, 0–2 on others). Pair it with top-p to cut the tail, but tune one knob at a time and evaluate on a fixed prompt set.

formula: p(token) = exp(z / T) / Σ exp(zⱼ / T)

mission.ui: time to break it on purpose. Drag the temperature to 2.5 and run 10 times. Bet the cat ends up somewhere weird.
mission.cmd: time to break it on purpose. Run with --temp 2.5 --times 10. Bet the cat ends up somewhere weird.

break.success: Nicely broken: “{tok}”. At high temperature the distribution goes almost flat and even absurd words get a shot. That’s how “creative” text is born… and nonsense too.
break.calm: At T={T}, everything still behaving. Turn the temperature up or run again: a lottery is a lottery.

ui: Drag the temperature control and hit the orange button.
For the most predictable result, push the control all the way left.
cmd: Temperature goes at the end of the command, after --temp.
For the most predictable result, use the smallest value there is.

errors.missingFlag.temp: You left out the temperature. Without it, most APIs use the default (usually 1), so the result changes every run. Add --temp 0 at the end.
errors.notNumber.temp: “{value}” isn’t a number, and the model doesn’t take adjectives here. Temperature goes from 0 (predictable) to 2 (chaotic). Try --temp 0.7.
errors.belowMin.temp: Negative temperature? Bold. But scores get divided by the temperature: with a negative number the ranking flips and “microwave” becomes the favorite. That’s why APIs refuse it.
errors.aboveMax.temp: Easy there, Prometheus. Above 2 almost every API refuses, and this simulator stops at 5. Try something between 0 and 2.
errors.notNumber.times: “{value}” isn’t a number of times. Use a whole number, like --times 10.
errors.notInteger.times: You can’t run half a time. Use a whole number, like --times 10.
errors.belowMin.times: Running zero times is the cheapest way to use AI, but it teaches nothing. Try --times 10.
errors.aboveMax.times: Up to 20 at a time. Beyond that the cat asks for overtime, and 10 already shows the variation nicely.

moods: Chaos: most APIs won’t even allow it
scene.bagCaption: Each color is a word; more marbles, more chance. Temperature is how hard the bag shakes before you grab the top one.
scene.bagAria: Bag of colored marbles; the higher the temperature, the more mixed they get
scene.barsNote: The bars change as you adjust the temperature. Orange = the word drawn in the last run.
scene.otherPrompt: In this simulator only the cat has computed probabilities. In recipe mode you can test any sentence.

steps: Open the playground (or API) of the AI provider you use.
Write the prompt: Complete with one word: “The cat climbed onto the…”.
Set temperature to 0 and send it three times. Then repeat with temperature at its maximum.
recipe.ok: at 0, three identical answers (or nearly; the Expert level explains the “nearly”). At max, varied and sometimes odd answers.
